sources.excerpt: Fulltone 70 Pedal-BC | AllThePedals Articles Genealogy Browse Search results for " " Gain / Fuzz / Fulltone 70 Pedal-BC 70 Pedal-BC The Fulltone '70 Pedal-BC delivers aggressive fuzz with a raw, vintage vibe. Featuring mismatched silicon transistors for a snarling, spitting tone, it's designed for players seeking authentic '70s fuzz sounds. With its mid control, the '70 Pedal-BC provides extra clarity and cut, and offers a unique character ideal for classic rock and blues. Compared to the '69 Pedal , the '70 pedal goes further with its raw, untamed sound. What Fulltone say about the 70 Pedal-BC Ever played an original FuzzFace from around 1970? (HINT: Not AT ALL the same sound as ones with the same namesake being mass-produced currently.) Ours has two intentionally mismatched (for harmonic content) silicon transistors that snarl and spit... not for the meek! If you put the "Fuzz" on 10 you will rip, and you might get all sorts of oscillation and weirdness... but that's Rock. Don't try using it with a wah wah... you can't, and neither could Jimi, without it screaming and howling. You want polite and quiet? Go elsewhere. You want art in a box? Come on in. Housed in a 16 gauge steel box and powder coated deep blue, this pedal is a bit unruly but with some warmth... ideal for older 4 input Marshall amps, it has much more FUZZ than the '69 Pedal and includes a Mid control for extra clarity and cut. I got my hands on Eric Johnson's Blue Fuzzface that he used from Tones through Ah Via Musicom period (now owned by Ian Moore) and incorporated a few of its tonal secrets into the '70 pedal with staggering sonic results! www.fulltoneusa.com 70 Pedal-BC compared to ... 70 Pedal-BC Fulltone Link 70 Pedal-BC Type Fuzz - Popularity - Average Price - - Status Unknown - Genealogy Our Genealogy Project attempts to create a family tree of all gain effects by mapping the pedal(s) that directly preceded them. The "Fulltone 70 PEDAL-BC" recreates the classic 70s fuzz! 1 Sparkplug.tokyo 2025年1月14日 09:21 Fulltone 70 PEDAL-BC Fuzz Pedal The Fulltone 70 PEDAL-BC is a faithful recreation of a classic early 1970s fuzz pedal, adding warmth to the classic fuzz tone. The intense fuzz generated by two intentionally mismatched silicon transistors pairs perfectly with vintage 4-input Marshall amplifiers. Based on the signature sound of the Blue Fuzzface used by Eric Johnson during his "Ah Via Musicom" era, it has been refined for modern players. 🔗 Fulltone 70 Pedal-BC ✅ Silicon Transistors: Equipped with two mismatched silicon transistors to recreate a warm, thick fuzz tone. ✅ Mid Control: An adjustable midrange provides a fuzz sound with great cut and clarity. ✅ Eric Johnson's Blue Fuzzface: Inspired by Eric Johnson's legendary Blue Fuzzface, pursuing the sound of his "Tones" and "Ah Via Musicom" eras. Perfect for those who want to enjoy a warm, classic fuzz tone with vintage Marshall amps, or for those who want to add personality to their solos and leads with a high-fuzz sound. It was founded in 1991 by talented musician and engineer Michael Fuller. With revolutionary and highly reliable pedals, it established its position as a prominent brand in the music industry. Fulltone has always provided products that meet the musical needs of professional musicians and enthusiasts, with a deep passion for music and a commitment to craftsmanship. Each pedal is a handmade USA-made pedal designed with meticulous attention to detail, ensuring superior sound quality and durability. Fulltone pedals are highly acclaimed for their organic tone, excellent manufacturing quality, and intuitive user interface, and are loved by guitarists all over the world. However, in 2022, Mike Fuller ceased operations in California for various reasons. Fulltone USA from 2024 In 2023, Brad Jackson (Jackson Audio and Jackson Ampworks) contacted Mike about licensing Fulltone Musical Products under the name Fulltone USA, resulting in a partnership. At Winter NAMM 2024, Fulltone USA took over product design, manufacturing, support, and sales, and started in earnest under the Fulltone USA name in collaboration with Mike Fuller.
